=== THE CENTRAL CLAIM, AND IT HOLDS ===
The fix is one line: add --first-parent to the single `git log` call inside resolve_reviewable_head(). I verified BOTH halves of the claim independently.

1. THE BUG IS REAL. Before touching this branch I built the scenario from scratch in a throwaway repo (mainline content commit dated 2026-01-02, a side branch whose content commit is dated LATER at 2026-06-01, then `git merge -s ours --no-ff` whose first-parent diff is empty so #56's _is_record_only_commit correctly skips it). Driving both variants of the real module against it:
       with    --first-parent -> the MAINLINE commit   (correct)
       without --first-parent -> the SIDE-branch commit (wrong)
   So plain `git log`'s date-ordered traversal really does leave mainline and return a commit that is not part of what the branch's review is meant to cover. The PR's diagnosis is accurate, and the date-ordering dependence explains the platform-specific flake (windows red, ubuntu/macos green) without hand-waving.

2. THE NEW TEST IS NOT VACUOUS, AND IT IS DETERMINISTIC. This is the part that matters most, because this repository has shipped vacuous checks before -- including a test written to catch vacuous checks that was itself vacuous. MUTATION PROBE: I removed --first-parent from scripts/lwb_lanes.py on this branch and ran the new test 10 times: 10/10 FAILED. Restored, it passes. Then the full suite under the same mutant: exactly ONE test fails -- test_reviewable_head_walks_first_parent_only_not_a_later_dated_side_commit, the one this PR adds. So the PR's "red before / green after, 10x each way" claim is confirmed by my own measurement, and the new test is the ONLY thing in the repository that detects the loss of this fix.
   Notably, the pre-existing #56 test (test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff) did NOT fail under the mutant on Linux. That independently corroborates the PR's account of WHY a new test was needed rather than relying on the old one: the old test reproduces the defect only by wall-clock luck. The PR did not overstate this.
   The test is deterministic by construction, not by luck: dates are pinned via GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE with explicit +00:00 offsets (so it is timezone-independent, not merely clock-independent). Better still, it ASSERTS ITS OWN PREMISE -- `assert plain_order.index(side) < plain_order.index(substantive)` and `assert side not in first_parent_order` -- so if the setup ever stops reproducing the condition the test is guarding, it fails loudly instead of passing for the wrong reason. That is the correct defence against the vacuity hazard, applied by the author without being asked.

=== a07ff98 IS AN HONESTY FIX, AND I CHECKED IT IS NOT AN ESCAPE HATCH ===
a07ff98 flips one command in proof/63.json from `verifiable: true` to `verifiable: false` / `nondeterministic-output`. That command is a pytest invocation whose recorded tail is "2 passed, 79 deselected in 0.71s" -- it embeds an ELAPSED TIME, so its digest can never reproduce. The previous `verifiable: true` was therefore a false claim that would have failed re-execution; marking it non-verifiable is the correct correction, not a dodge.
I checked whether the honest fix should instead have been to sanitise the timing away, which would have kept the command verifiable: scripts/lwb_sanitise.py normalises absolute paths ONLY -- it has no timing normalisation at all. So under the current sanitiser NO pytest invocation can ever be verifiable, and `verifiable: false` is a truthful description of reality rather than an opt-out this PR invented. I also confirmed this record does not become vacuously unverifiable: 3 of its 6 commands are still verifiable and all 3 re-execute and PASS (lwb_build.py --check, lwb_check_prefix.py, lwb_check_no_instruction_dep.py).
OBSERVATION, not a charge against this PR: the consequence is that the proof-of-completion mechanism can never re-verify the single most important piece of evidence any deliverable offers -- its test suite passing. That is a limitation of the sanitiser, on main, and it is directly relevant to in-flight PR #62 (make lwb-proof-reexecute blocking), which would make a gate blocking while every pytest command in the repository is structurally exempt from it.

=== A METHODOLOGICAL DEFECT IN MY OWN DISPATCH INSTRUCTIONS ===
My routine's step 4 tells me to skip any PR whose reviews/<pr>/ holds a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA. That test is WRONG. scripts/lwb_lanes.py compares reviewed_commit against resolve_reviewable_head(), which deliberately skips reviews/- and proof/-only commits, so a record-only commit advances the raw head while leaving the record perfectly valid. Measured across all 18 open PRs this run: 0 of 18 had a record naming the raw head, but 16 of 18 had a valid record naming the REVIEWABLE head. Following step 4 literally would have meant re-reviewing 16 already-reviewed PRs, each of my own record-only pushes re-advancing the raw head -- a routine that never converges. Only #53 and #63 genuinely lacked a current record. Recommend step 4 compare against resolve_reviewable_head(). This PR is the one that makes that function trustworthy, which is a pointed coincidence.
